items.text: On the Solemnity of Christ the King, Pope Leo XIV said at the Angelus that Christ reveals the true meaning of justice. He called the Last Judgement a word of salvation and a proclamation of mercy, and said Christ is not a despot who threatens but the true King who redeems.

After the Angelus, the Pope prayed for victims of conflicts worldwide and urged leaders to seek reconciliation and peace without delay. He voiced closeness to Papua New Guinea and other Pacific countries hit by El Niño drought, and asked young people marking World Youth Day in their dioceses to be gentle and humble like Christ, looking ahead to Seoul 2027.

For the tenth World Day of the Poor, Pope Leo XIV shared lunch with about 1,300 people in need in the Paul VI Hall, telling them, "Today, we are all one family." More than 400 Italian Red Cross volunteers served the meal, and guests came through Rome charities.

Cambridge Dictionary named "human" its Word of the Year for 2026, citing global debates over what it means to be human as AI blurs the line between people and machines. Its announcement quotes Pope Leo XIV's letter Magnifica humanitas on the "pressing duty to remain profoundly human."

EWTN premiered its first late-night-style comedy talk show, It's Not Too Late with Paul Laudiero, on Nov. 20. The hourlong family-friendly program streams free on EWTN+ and EWTN.com every other Friday at 6 p.m. ET.

Catholics in Mexico City are marking 100 years since the start of the Cristero War with two Christ the King processions: a Blessed Sacrament procession at the Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe on Nov. 21 and a procession through the historic center to the Metropolitan Cathedral on Nov. 22. A jubilee year honoring the Cristero witnesses opens Nov. 22, with a plenary indulgence available.

The EU bishops' commission COMECE issued a position paper on Nov. 20 opposing the erasure of baptismal records at the request of people who leave the Church. It responds to an EU Court of Justice advocate general's opinion in a case against the Diocese of Ghent, and argues that a baptismal record documents a sacramental event rather than a person's current beliefs.

Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, the Holy See's foreign minister, urged the international community at the MED Dialogues in Naples to redouble its efforts for Lebanon, calling the country crucial for democracy in the region and for the continued Christian presence in the Middle East. He voiced concern about the future of the UNIFIL mission.

World Jewish Congress president Ronald Lauder met Pope Leo XIV on Nov. 20 for their first private audience. He thanked the Pope for his condemnations of antisemitism, proposed joint education for young Jews and Catholics, and called for Church-Jewish cooperation, including with senior technology leaders, to put humanity first in the development of artificial intelligence.

Pope Leo XIV told more than 6,000 young people from Italy's Lazio region in the Paul VI Hall that Christ knows each of them by name and that holiness is a gift, not a performance that causes stress. Answering their questions at an event on the theme of World Youth Day Seoul 2027, he urged them to read the Gospel daily and walk with the Church community.

Meeting members of the Vienna Philharmonic, in Rome for the 25th International Festival of Music and Sacred Art (November 21 to 25), Pope Leo said that in an age of wars and mistrust, music teaches people to listen to one another and that human beings are not destined to remain locked in competitive opposition.

The Catholic University of America hosted the 2026 Symposium for the Advancement of Catholic Health Care on November 21, on Magnifica humanitas, artificial intelligence and Catholic health care. Sessions included Charles Camosy and Velatura's chief AI officer Prashant Natarajan on whether Catholic health systems should build their own AI, and OpenAI's James Hairston on bridging AI, health care and Catholic teaching.

Pope Leo XIV named French Dominican Fr. Serge-Thomas Bonino, president of the Pontifical Academy of St. Thomas Aquinas since 2014 and former secretary general of the International Theological Commission, as Theologian of the Papal Household. The Pope also gave the personal title of archbishop to Msgr. Aurelio García Macías, secretary of the Dicastery for Divine Worship, and Msgr. Paul Tighe, secretary of the Dicastery for Culture and Education, and named Msgr. Javier Domingo Fernández González nuncio to Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Pope Leo approved decrees clearing Blessed Zdenka Schelingová, a Slovak Sister of Charity of the Holy Cross who suffered under the Communist regime in Czechoslovakia, for canonization, and Venerable Rosa Staltari for beatification. Decrees also recognize the martyrdom of Fr. José Gómez Llor and 54 companions killed in the Spanish Civil War, and declare Venerable two priests, Angelo Lolli and Abundio García Román, and 14-year-old Giulia Gabrieli.

Receiving delegations from the International Astronautical Federation and the Italian Space Agency ahead of the International Space Forum in Rome on Monday, Pope Leo urged that outer space be kept from any non-peaceful use and said those who wage war and ruin creation are blinded by the idols of power and money.

Pope Leo XIV will have lunch on Sunday, Nov. 22, with about 1,300 poor and vulnerable people in the Paul VI Hall for the tenth World Day of the Poor. The lunch was moved back a week because of his Latin America trip. This year Rome's soup kitchens and shelters will also serve a meal 'in communion' with the Pope. Donors include a Spanish company that gave turkeys for about 2,000 people and a town in Poland that sent hams.

At the U.S. bishops' Nov. 18 session on how young adults seek faith, Archbishop Thomas Wenski of Miami said that if secularism brought disenchantment, the young may be on 'a search for re-enchantment,' which he sees in those who kneel for Communion and 'insist on going to Latin Mass.' CUA sociologist Brandon Vaidyanathan replied that Gen Z, unlike millennials, is asking whether the Church was 'too hasty' to abandon some traditional forms. A clip of the exchange circulated widely overnight.

The 13 Discalced Carmelite nuns of the Monastery of St. Teresa in Florence use AI to draw MonachIA, an anime-style cartoon nun. On Instagram she shares the Gospel, the saints and daily cloistered life with more than 18,000 followers. The project began as a way to support the monastery's handmade-goods shop and now brings in hundreds of prayer requests. The sisters say the name makes the use of AI clear.

UEFA fined England's Football Association 15,000 euros and gave it a one-match away-ticket ban, suspended for two years, after anti-Catholic chants by England fans at the Nov. 15 Nations League match in Madrid. The FA called the chanting 'unacceptable and deeply offensive.'

Clergy abuse survivors in the Archdiocese of New Orleans have begun receiving payments from the $305 million bankruptcy settlement. Settlement trustee Don Massey confirmed on Nov. 20 that $180 million has reached 450 of roughly 740 survivors, and said the trust aims to pay the rest by year's end while it waits on hundreds of distribution forms. The archdiocese filed for bankruptcy in May 2020.

Pope Leo XIV will meet about 100 figures from the cycling world at the Vatican on Monday, Nov. 23, including Eddy Merckx, Greg LeMond, Chris Froome and 20-year-old Paul Seixas. The event is organized by the Dicastery for Culture and Education with the Union Cycliste Internationale, which will donate bicycles to Caritas Rome.

After Wednesday's general audience, Pope Leo XIV prayed with relatives of people who were abducted, killed and secretly buried during the Troubles in Northern Ireland. Archbishop Eamon Martin brought them to Rome and asked anyone with information to come forward so the remaining families can give their loved ones a Christian burial. Thirteen of the disappeared have been recovered since 1998.

On Nov. 14, three men tied up Melkite Archbishop Jean-Abdo Arbach in his office in Homs, Syria, and stole his pectoral cross and money. He is safe. The Greek Orthodox, Syriac Orthodox and Melkite patriarchs in Damascus issued a joint statement condemning repeated attacks and ransom kidnappings and the authorities' failure to protect people, while affirming their commitment to living with their Muslim neighbors as equal citizens.
Msgr. Pablo Colino, the Spanish priest who directed St. Peter's Cappella Giulia choir from 1980 to 2006, died Nov. 18 at 92, the same day as the basilica's 400th anniversary.

The Holy See submitted a working paper on lethal autonomous weapons to the Seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva (Nov. 16-20). It calls for a moratorium and a legally binding framework, arguing that machines calculate while humans judge, so life-and-death decisions cannot be handed to algorithms, and that responsibility can never be shifted to the machine.

More than 6,000 young people from the dioceses of Lazio will meet Pope Leo XIV in the Paul VI Hall on Saturday, Nov. 21, for a regional World Youth Day under the Seoul 2027 theme, "Take courage! I have overcome the world." The Pope will answer five questions from the young people.

Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, told Vatican media that the Church in the Holy Land brings hope where politics does not reach. He said the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dramatic and that Cardinal Claudio Gugerotti's visit expresses Pope Leo's closeness to Christians there.

Pope Leo XIV received the Catholic Near East Welfare Association (CNEWA) on Nov. 20 for its 100th anniversary. Founded by Pius XI in 1926, the agency supports the Eastern Churches of the Middle East, northeast Africa, India and Eastern Europe. The Pope said accompanying Eastern Christians in their homelands is an essential work of hope: when a Christian family is forced to leave, a community is weakened and a living tradition is put at risk, but suffering and uncertainty do not have the last word.

This year's Christmas tree for St. Peter's Square, a 24-meter (about 78-foot) silver fir from the Cugno dell'Acero forest in Italy's Pollino National Park, arrived at the Vatican on Nov. 19 as a gift from Terranova di Pollino. Children receiving cancer treatment in Italian hospitals will light it on Dec. 7 at 5:30 p.m. Rome time, while a tree is lit at the same moment in Gubbio for the 800th anniversary of the death of St. Francis.

In an interview with America, Matthew Harvey Sanders, founder and CEO of Longbeard, the company behind Magisterium AI and the Vulgate digitization project with pontifical universities in Rome, said moving ahead with AI is absolutely worth the risk, citing the hope of curing disease and helping the world's poor escape scarcity. He said his confidence rests not in the tool but in people learning to use it well, adding: I'm a Christian; that's why I'm hopeful. He also called the rush to deploy poorly understood AI into critical systems a mistake and said the greater risk is an economy that leaves little place for human work.

Cardinal Fabio Baggio joined Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith on the Tools and Weapons podcast to discuss Pope Leo XIV's encyclical Magnifica humanitas and the Church's response to AI, including human dignity, the future of work, equitable access and the risk of new forms of servitude. The conversation centers on how to ensure technology serves humanity rather than the other way around.

A Gallup survey for The Catholic University of America, presented to the U.S. bishops in Baltimore, found that nearly two-thirds of young adult Catholics say religion has become more important to them in the last five years, and 82 percent of those cite an encounter with beauty in religious spaces or rituals as an important factor. Practice lags behind: only about a quarter of young adult Catholics attend Mass weekly, and for every adult convert, 8.4 adults raised Catholic leave the Church.

The Nebraska-based Catholic Mutual Relief Society of America has asked a federal court to declare that it has no remaining obligation to cover sexual abuse claims against several Louisiana dioceses, including Baton Rouge and Lafayette, saying earlier limited coverage has been exhausted and that it ended its Louisiana contracts in 2024. The Diocese of Alexandria, now in bankruptcy, is excluded from the suit.

By a Vatican decree, the Archdiocese of Miami will assume pastoral and canonical care of the roughly 9,000 Catholics of the Cayman Islands, which the Archdiocese of Detroit has overseen as a mission sui iuris since 2000. The community includes a parish, a parochial school and two mission communities.

St. Peter's Basilica has opened a Living Archive that uses artificial intelligence to let scholars, pilgrims and visitors explore twenty years of archival research on more than 200 painters, mosaicists and illuminators who worked there between 1503 and 1667. Built with Microsoft on the basilica's digital twin, the tool does not generate content but retrieves and connects material verified by the Fabric of St. Peter, always citing sources. Archbishop Vittorio Francesco Viola said discernment and evaluation remain human responsibilities and that AI should encourage critical thinking.

The Vatican's Dicastery for Communication will host a free Zoom webinar, open to everyone, on Nov. 26 from 2:30 to 4:30 p.m. Rome time, titled Using AI as a human amplifier. Prof. Antonio Cisternino of the University of Pisa will present, and registration is required.

Pope Leo XIV received about 3,000 members of the Shalom Catholic Community, founded in Brazil, for its 45th anniversary on Nov. 19. He said their peace is rooted in an encounter with the Risen Christ and urged them to accompany young people, who still seek genuine love, authentic beauty and God, toward an encounter with Jesus, in communion with the Church's pastors.

Jesuit High School in New Orleans is marking what it believes is the 100th year of its Thanksgiving Drive. Students, faculty, alumni and parents are preparing food baskets for about 640 families, which will be blessed at a prayer service and delivered the day before Thanksgiving.

The U.S. bishops voted at their Baltimore meeting to update the conference's investment guidelines. The new rules bar investment in private prisons and detention facilities and add an AI section: no investing in companies making autonomous weapons or targeting systems without meaningful human oversight, AI designed to be addictive or manipulative or to harm the mental health of young or vulnerable people, or surveillance that violates dignity and privacy. The guidelines also lean on shareholder advocacy to press AI firms on deepfakes, pornography, privacy and workers' rights, and flag concerns about cryptocurrency and prediction markets. Bishop Oscar Cantú said his AI task force will prioritize opening the public conversation, with webinars where bishops hear directly from engineers about both benefits and risks.

Pope Leo XIV received participants in a Caritas Internationalis meeting marking 25 years of COATnet, a network of more than 30 Christian organizations fighting human trafficking. Recalling his years in Peru, he urged them not to lose the joy of being God's hands and instruments of a peace that is unarmed and disarming, and said it is faith that distinguishes their mission.
Organizers of World Youth Day 2027 in Seoul released four sign-language versions of the official theme song to make the gathering more accessible to young people with disabilities.

Soulton Hall, an English country house built during the Reformation, hosted the first public Mass in its history on Nov. 14. Prior Matthew Jarvis OP celebrated it in the Dominican Rite on the feast of the Translation of St Erkenwald.

Joseph Liu Hengping, 54, was ordained Bishop of Xiamen in Fujian, China, on Nov. 18 under the Holy See-China agreement, after Pope Leo appointed him on Oct. 15. The diocese had been without its own bishop for nearly two years.

New Orleans Archbishop Checchio calls Advent a season of hope amid darkness and urges extra time for prayer so Christmas busyness does not crowd out Christ. His column also reprints his letter on the abuse crisis and the coming records archive with Louisiana State University.

The U.S. bishops voted 205-0 to rewrite their 2001 pastoral plan for pro-life activities, citing the end of Roe, abortion pills, assisted suicide and IVF. Papal nuncio Archbishop Gabriele Caccia urged the new plan to push for a ban on surrogacy.
The bishops also voted 180-15, with 7 abstentions, to make the last Sunday of October an annual day of prayer for racial justice.

The Vatican's worship dicastery upheld Charlotte Bishop Michael Martin's ban on altar rails and kneelers at Communion, while noting the faithful may still kneel to receive and may not be refused Communion for it.

Bishop Oscar Cantu said the Church must become a school of discernment in the digital age, noted there are responsible ways to use AI in Church offices, and said the Holy See has asked for internal AI policies; the firm rule is no private information in chatbots.

Bishop Oscar Cantú of San Jose updated the U.S. bishops in Baltimore on their new Task Force on Preserving Human Dignity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence, telling them the Church can have neither naive enthusiasm nor unfounded fear about AI and asking for their ideas on the task force's work. The task force, which met in person for the first time on Nov. 15, has met engineers from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google and plans internal AI guidelines for Catholic institutions and webinars for bishops, church leaders and parishes.

items.text: The U.S. bishops approved a new Lectionary for Mass and Book of the Gospels aligned with the forthcoming Catholic American Bible; it still needs confirmation from the Vatican's Dicastery for Divine Worship. They also renewed the Resolution on Diocesan Financial Reporting through 2031 by a vote of 205-2-1.

Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass for the 400th anniversary of the dedication of St. Peter's Basilica, saying its doors open to the world with the invitation "Come, enter, taste!" and that war, misery, error and despair do not prevail so long as the Church proclaims peace, charity, truth and salvation.

A Russian drone exploded in front of the Roman Catholic Cathedral of the Assumption in central Odesa, Ukraine, on Nov. 18, breaking about half of its large windows and damaging its doors and the diocesan curia next door. Cathedral and curia staff were unhurt; four people died and about ten were injured in the city's attacks that morning.

Cardinal Michael Czerny, presenting Pope Leo XIV's encyclical Magnifica humanitas in Sofia, said decisions to use lethal force must stay in human hands, with a traceable chain of responsibility, time for human judgment, and protection of civilians.

At the USCCB meeting in Baltimore, Archbishop Paul Coakley said waiting for pre-marriage classes is too late and backed the Vatican's marriage catechumenate starting in youth ministry; Bishop Daniel Flores said young people need renewed hope that love lasts.

At his first General Audience since returning from Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Pope Leo XIV said he felt at home in Chiclayo, and in his appeals marked Italy's Day of Prayer for Victims and Survivors of Abuse, calling prevention a way of living out evangelical conversion.
Pope Leo XIV presides at Mass in St. Peter's Basilica today, Nov. 18, at 5 p.m. Rome time, marking 400 years since Pope Urban VIII dedicated the current basilica in 1626.

At the U.S. bishops' fall assembly in Baltimore, Bishop Daniel Flores of Brownsville presented the U.S. Church's part in the Intercontinental Guadalupan Novena, the multi-year preparation for the 500th anniversary of the apparitions of Our Lady of Guadalupe in 2031, along with the 'One Tilma, One Heart' initiative.

The patriarchs and heads of churches in Syria, including Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarch Youssef Absi, issued a joint statement on Nov. 17 condemning continuing attacks, kidnappings and intimidation against Christians and asking the authorities to protect citizens and investigate.

In France, Bishop Renauld de Dinechin of Luçon has told a priest of the Institute of the Good Shepherd to stop celebrating the Traditional Latin Mass and holding catechism at the private Chapel of the Holy Family at the Château de Ramberge in the Vendée, where the old Mass had been offered since 1983 for up to 300 people each Sunday. His Oct. 25 letter was made public on Nov. 17.

Meeting in Baltimore, the U.S. bishops voted to advance the cause of beatification and canonization of Maria Middleton, a Bucks County, Pennsylvania, teenager who died of an inoperable brain tumor in 2020 at age 18. Bishop Thomas Paprocki said reports of intercessory graces have come from the U.S., Italy, Poland and Uganda. The Archdiocese of Philadelphia now opens the diocesan phase of the inquiry.

Apostolic nuncio Archbishop Gabriele Caccia told the bishops to prepare for their 2027 ad limina visits to Rome in the spirit of Blessed Fulton Sheen, with the humility to examine their ministry honestly and openness to renewed love for the Church, and to bring signs of hope such as the number of adult catechumens. He noted they will meet the first pope 'speaking with an American accent.'

Speaking for Pope Leo XIV at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin urged delegates to keep the people most affected by climate change at the center, calling it a matter of justice, and proposed an educational pact putting human dignity and the common good at the heart of the climate agenda.

The U.S. bishops opened the public sessions of their fall plenary assembly in Baltimore with a message to Pope Leo XIV. In his first presidential address, Archbishop Paul Coakley urged bishops not to read Church life through political or ideological lenses, saying the Church thinks in terms of mission, and pointed to a shared hope rooted in human dignity amid the challenges and opportunities of artificial intelligence.

The bishops elected Bishop Kevin Rhoades of Fort Wayne-South Bend as conference secretary (157-59 over Bishop Earl Fernandes) and Fr. Paul Hartmann of Milwaukee as general secretary. Chairmen-elect: Bishop James Conley (Catholic Education), Bishop Louis Tylka (Communications), Bishop Michael Pham (Cultural Diversity), Bishop William Joensen (Doctrine), Bishop Gerald Vincke (National Collections) and Bishop Donald Hying (Pro-Life Activities, 113-104 over Bishop John Folda).

At a press conference, Archbishop Coakley said the bishops are ready to work with the new Democratic-controlled Congress on the common good, while Vice President Bishop Daniel Flores said concerns about a de facto mass deportation policy and due process for migrants remain real.

Austria's bishops adopted their first comprehensive guidelines for artificial intelligence in Church life at their Salzburg plenary. AI may assist with tasks such as homily preparation and administration, but in sacraments, preaching, liturgy and pastoral care it may only be supportive and may not replace personal relationships. Every diocese will name a person responsible for AI, coordinated by a national working group.

In an interview with Crux, Matthew Harvey Sanders, CEO of Longbeard, which builds Magisterium AI and Vulgate, called AI potentially "one of the greatest vehicles for evangelization in history." He said skepticism is healthy as discernment but "becomes costly when it turns into absence," named false affection, dependence on systems with a different worldview, and forgery as the main risks, and proposed a Vatican-backed benchmark of how faithful AI models are to Church teaching. Magisterium AI answers from Church documents with a citation on every point. Crux notes Longbeard has long sponsored the outlet.

On the flight from Lima to Rome after his 12-day journey to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Pope Leo XIV told journalists that Traditionis Custodes, Pope Francis' 2021 restriction on the pre-conciliar Latin Mass, will stay in force: "we will continue to follow that." He noted that it allows dispensations for the Vetus Ordo and that "there is an avenue available for those who wish to apply." Asked by Le Figaro, he said a document on spiritual abuse is being studied but none is imminent, and he had no comment on new cardinals.

In the same press conference, the Pope said ordaining married men, proposed at the 2019 Amazon synod, is "not the only solution" and could cause division, adding that some things may change in the future. He said he is "not at 100 percent" but doing well a month after his October 13 surgery, and called for dialogue and less polarization after the US midterm elections.

Archbishop Nelson Perez of Philadelphia has received a formal petition to open a sainthood cause for Maria Middleton, a Doylestown teenager who died of brain cancer in 2020 at age 18. On Nov. 16 he issued an edict asking for her writings and any information about her reputation for holiness, and the U.S. bishops will be consulted on the cause at their Baltimore assembly this week.

In the Diocese of Lafayette, Louisiana, former parish priest Michael Guidry, 83, was released from state prison over the weekend after completing a seven-year sentence for molesting a teenage altar server at St. Peter's in Morrow. The diocese has restricted him from public ministry; the victim's father, former deacon Scott Peyton, lost a Vatican appeal of his excommunication in October.

ZENIT reports OpenAI data showing about 70 million religion-related ChatGPT requests a week, with roughly half of Christianity-related questions about understanding biblical passages. ZENIT's analysis calls it neither cause for automatic enthusiasm nor blanket rejection, but an opportunity for the Church to lead people from the screen toward Scripture, community and pastoral guidance.

Pope Leo XIV closed his South America journey with Mass at Las Palmas Air Base in Lima, attended by about 1.5 million people by local estimates. "My journey is coming to an end, but the mission continues," he said, sending the faithful to proclaim the true God. During the popemobile tour a small rosary thrown from the crowd struck him; Vatican News said he was unharmed.

After a farewell ceremony, the papal plane left Callao at 2:28 p.m. local time, ending the Nov. 6-16 visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It is due at Rome's Fiumicino airport Tuesday at 10:25 a.m. Rome time.

The U.S. bishops opened their fall plenary assembly in Baltimore with prayer and a Mass celebrated by USCCB president Archbishop Paul S. Coakley at the Baltimore Basilica. Public sessions on Nov. 17-18 will include an update from the new Task Force on Preserving Human Dignity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence, an immigration update, elections, and a vote on a new edition of the Lectionary.

The Archdiocese of New Orleans has come out against Mayor Helena Moreno's proposed parcel fee on tax-exempt properties to fund drainage, roads and other infrastructure. Spokesperson Sarah McDonald said any fee on archdiocesan properties would hurt parishes, schools and ministries; the city hopes to bring a plan to voters in 2027, raising $10 million to $15 million in its first year.

Bishop Renauld de Dinechin of Luçon, France, has asked Father Jean Cuchet of the Institute of the Good Shepherd to stop celebrating the Traditional Latin Mass at the private Ramberge chapel in La Gaubretière, Vendée, where it had been offered since 1983. In an Oct. 25 letter he cited Traditionis custodes, declined canonical recognition, and pointed the 150 to 300 weekly faithful to four approved sites nearby.

A study in Sociological Inquiry found 28.8 percent of 1,049 U.S. Catholics believe the bread and wine truly become the Body and Blood of Christ, essentially unchanged from 2019 and 1992 polls despite the bishops' Eucharistic Revival. Belief was about 60 percent among weekly Mass-goers. The U.S. bishops meet in Baltimore Nov. 17-18.

Pope Leo XIV ends his 12-day South America journey on Monday. Back in Lima late Sunday after Cusco and Pucallpa, he greeted crowds from the apostolic nunciature balcony. Monday he visits elderly residents cared for by the Little Sisters of the Abandoned Elderly in Callao, celebrates the closing Mass at Las Palmas Air Base, where more than a million people are expected, and departs for Rome at 1:45 p.m. Lima time, landing at Fiumicino Tuesday morning.

Thirty-six bishops of Ecuador begin their ad limina visit to Rome, November 16 to 20, opening with Mass at St. John Lateran and meetings with Vatican dicasteries and the Pontifical Commission for the Protection of Minors. They meet Pope Leo XIV on Friday, November 20.

Ateneo de Davao University, a Jesuit Catholic university in the Philippines, issued a University Policy on the Ethical, Humane, and Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (Circular 2026-0008, dated November 11). President Fr. Karel San Juan, SJ, wrote that, guided by Ignatian discernment, AI use must strengthen intellectual effort, conscience, creativity, and relationships, with human purpose and judgment guiding it at every stage.

In Pucallpa, in the Peruvian Amazon, Pope Leo XIV met missionaries and representatives of Amazonian peoples. He said protecting the rainforest cannot be separated from care for the people who live there, condemned the murders of Indigenous leaders, illegal mining, oil spills and drug trafficking, voiced concern for women and girls facing violence and abuse, and noted that the local vicariate, as large as entire countries, has only 25 priests.

At the closing Mass in Pucallpa, Pope Leo urged young people especially to cultivate the grandeur of humanity, saying that doing good means combating violence with charity and corruption with honesty. Afterward he prayed before the image of the Immaculate Conception, whom he called Mother of the Amazon.

Lithuanian police identified a British citizen born in 1989 as the suspect after a golden figure of Christ was taken from a cross in the courtyard of the Divine Mercy Shrine in Vilnius on November 11 and smashed in the street. His identity document was seized and prosecutors are investigating it as desecration of a place of public reverence.

Pope Leo XIV spent Sunday in Cusco, Peru. At Saqsaywaman, before a crowd EWTN News put at about 100,000, he met representatives of popular piety and gave a Golden Rose to the Virgin of Belén, the city's patroness, his second Golden Rose of the Peru visit. At the Angelus outside Cusco's cathedral he called the idea that illness diminishes a person's worth 'a great lie' of the throwaway culture, offered a shroud for the image of the Lord of the Earthquakes, remembered the late Archbishop Richard Alarcón, and greeted the new archbishop, Lizardo Estrada. He then flew to Pucallpa in the Peruvian Amazon to meet missionaries and representatives of Amazonian peoples, followed by Mass.

items.text: At St. Peter's Basilica, the Mass for the 10th World Day of the Poor was celebrated in the Pope's name by Archbishop Luis Marín de San Martín, identified by EWTN News as prefect of the Dicastery for the Service of Charity. Preaching on the parable of the talents, he said the Eucharist cannot be celebrated while remaining indifferent to hunger, loneliness and injustice. About 1,500 food parcels were distributed afterward, and Pope Leo is scheduled to lunch with 1,300 people in need in the Paul VI Hall on November 22.

Pope Leo XIV said goodbye to Chiclayo, the Peruvian diocese he led as bishop from 2015 to 2023, asking that it remain a capital of friendship and also a land of faith, devotion and fidelity. The papal plane left Chiclayo at 8:00 a.m. local time for Cusco and Pucallpa, with popular piety, Indigenous peoples and Mass on the Sunday program before a return to Lima in the evening.

A Latinobarómetro study of 17 Latin American countries finds the share of people identifying as Catholic fell from 80 percent in 1995 to 55 percent today. Panama saw the sharpest drop, from 89 to 46 percent, while Mexico fell least, from 77 to 69 percent; Paraguay is now the most Catholic country at 82 percent.

Pope Leo XIV spends Sunday in Cusco and Pucallpa. In Cusco, 41 years after St. John Paul II's visit, he is to meet representatives of popular devotion at Saqsayhuaman and pray the Angelus in the main square; in Pucallpa, in the Peruvian Amazon, he is to meet missionaries.

Bishop Jose Elmer Mangalinao of Bayombong, Philippines, issued a pastoral statement opposing the US-led Pax Silica industrial project and large-scale mining, saying development must not sacrifice farmers, Indigenous peoples and rural communities. He asked parishes, schools and households to hang banners on November 16.
Pope Leo XIV named Father Oswaldo Enrique Mendez Marchena, vicar general of the Archdiocese of Barquisimeto, Venezuela, as auxiliary bishop of Barquisimeto.

Pope Leo XIV closed the Jubilee Year of St. Turibius of Mogrovejo at the saint's shrine in Zaña, Peru, where Turibius died in 1606. About 10,000 people attended and more than 300,000 lined the route. He expressed affection and closeness to Afro-Peruvians, recalling the Africans enslaved there, voiced sorrow for victims of crime and extortion, and urged people never to grow accustomed to the suffering of others. He leaves early Sunday for Cusco and Pucallpa.

Eight teams from Ukrainian Greek Catholic and Roman Catholic monastic and religious communities began a practical AI training program on Nov. 10, building tools for reports, internal documents, and charitable work. Organizers require human oversight, keep pastoral and personal data out of AI tools, and leave spiritual guidance and decisions to people.

At St. Joseph Oratory in Portland, Maine, which has offered the traditional Latin Mass exclusively for just over a year, about 250 people attend regularly and the average age is 35, according to The Maine Monitor.
